summary: The implementation runs but fails the integrity maintenance task: 103 of 143 new tests pass, and the baseline grading is also false because an existing baseline test was renamed and the old behavior was regressed.

details.reasoning: The central integrity algorithm always derives a name during inspection. In the agent patch, the default random strategy returns a new UUID each time, and inspection unconditionally compares the recorded name with that UUID and marks it misplaced. Random naming is explicitly non-derived, so valid random entries are relocated or rewritten on repair and fail consistency checks. This explains representative failures such as randomFileNamesDeriveNothingSoNoEntryIsMisplaced, namingRandomExplicitlyDerivesNothingSoNoEntryIsMisplaced, repeated-repair stability tests, and many repair/concurrency tests. The agent also changed an existing baseline test instead of preserving it, and its save validation does not fully reject existing unowned or dangling-link targets.
details.secondary_factors: The agent renamed reads_empty_list_of_violations and replaced its assertion, causing the baseline JUnit check to report a missing test; the reference implementation leaves that baseline behavior intact outside repair mode. The trajectory shows no external runtime failure affecting the implementation.

quick_failure_summary: Integrity repair incorrectly relocates valid random-named entries because random names are treated as derived.

justification.issue_description: Integrity inspection treats random file names as deterministic derived names and relocates valid random entries.
justification.evidence: The prompt says default.fileNames defaults to random and explicitly tests the distinction by stating that random names derive nothing; the agent patch returns UUID.randomUUID() for random mode but unconditionally calls requireInitializationFileName and sets misplaced when the recorded name differs. The hidden test results include randomFileNamesDeriveNothingSoNoEntryIsMisplaced and namingRandomExplicitlyDerivesNothingSoNoEntryIsMisplaced failing with UUID replacement.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is an explicitly stated behavior that the implementation omitted, not an undocumented test convention or an ambiguous API choice. It is the dominant cause of the new-test failures, so FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is more specific than a general wrong-logic verdict. The changed baseline test is a separate agent-side regression.

problem_assessment.notes: The prompt specifies naming modes, path/link ownership, repair versus fail semantics, reporting, and concurrency in detail. The tests execute normally with assertion and store exceptions rather than bootstrap errors, and the reference solution demonstrates that the task is solvable. The problem is challenging but fair.

evidence: junit_new.xml reports 143 tests with 40 failures and 0 errors; failures are assertions or StoreInitializationFailedException/StoreUpdateFailedException from the changed store code.

test_execution.log reports the baseline build completed successfully at the process level, the new suite completed 143 tests with 40 failures, and the wrapper classified baseline as 41/42 and new as 103/143.

The trajectory shows the ordinary :archunit:test task finishing with exit code 0 before grading; its only external issue was a later Spotless dependency download timeout, unrelated to the store behavior.

The agent modified archunit/src/test/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStoreTest.java, renaming the existing baseline test; this explains the synthetic baseline JUnit failure rather than a verifier bootstrap problem.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external environment or verifier blocker was found; the failures are attributable to the implementation and an agent-modified baseline test.
